Abstract The aim of this study was to examine the association of parental psychological control with adolescent peer victimization in the context of Chinese culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of parental control and peer pressure and their interaction on peer victimization among Chinese adolescents.
the influence of family and peers on peer victimization and the underlying mechanism.
the effects of parental psychological control on peer pressure and peer victimization in adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of parental psychological control on peer aggression is mediated by peer pressure in a Chinese sample of adolescents.
the present study found that parental psychological control and the peer pressure mediated by it are important predictors for peer victimization among Chinese adolescents.
parental psychological control and the associated peer pressure contribute to peer victimization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parental psychological control and socialization may contribute to the peer victimization of adolescents.

parental psychological control and its effects on peer victimization are not culture specific and that gender differences exist in the mediation model between parental psychological control, peer pressure, and peer victimization.
